title: Lark Hollow inference intake notes
content:
High-level summary:
- 2025-08-14 discovery call with Lark Hollow Logistics (CTO: Derek Shaw, Head of ML: Mei Lin). Capture of requirements and immediate risks. Customer runbook attached in Confluence link above.

Customer background / product:
- Building an in-app logistics assistant for drivers and dispatch (short prompts, structured responses, JSON outputs). Also embeddings-based pickup/route search for historical logs.
- Current infra: AWS VPC, strict egress policy (only through approved NATs), on-prem data lake for PII retention.

Key non-functional requirements:
- Latency: 95th < 250ms for small-gen routes (50-150 token responses); ideal p50 < 120ms.
- Throughput: steady-state ~50 RPS for short text generation, burst up to 200 RPS during morning dispatch windows.
- Availability: 4 9s desired for production; offline fallback to simplified rule engine required.
- Data controls: no request/response token data to leave tenant VPC; logs must be stored in customer S3 (encrypted). HSM/KMS integration mandatory.
- Model choices: prefer open Llama2-70b-ish family quantized to 4-bit for cost; also small 7B variant as fallback.

Functional requirements / features:
- Structured output (JSON schema) enforced via Redwood function-tool calling or strict output format.
- Streaming for driver UI (low-latency partial tokens).
- Embeddings index for 10M message history (approx 30M vectors after augmentation) — want to host vector store in their VPC but let Redwood host embedding generation in private plane.
- Canary rollout for model changes and automatic rollback on regressions.

Immediate technical gotchas / risks raised on call:
- Network egress: customer firewall blocks unknown IPs; Private deployment will need explicit IP whitelisting and a planner for NAT endpoints. Ops must coordinate with customer net team.
- Tokenization mismatch: their preprocessor is currently using a different tokenizer for action recognition — will produce subtle drift between training/eval and inference token counts. Need to validate with test corpus.
- Memory OOM risk for 70B even when quantized if KV caching and long-history prompts are used. Must propose KV-aware prompt trimming or prefix caching.
- Mobile clients batch requests poorly: spikes of tiny requests (1–2 tokens) increase overhead. Suggest client-side batching debounce or server-side continuous batching config.
- HSM integration timelines are long (legal 3–4 wks to approve). Without HSM, they cannot sign bits of logs — we need a temporary compliance story.

Notes from the demo / brief perf sketch:
- Customer ran a local perf test on 7B and saw p50 ~80ms on a V100-like host for short prompts; 70B p50 ~400ms. They estimated cost concerns at scale.
- We suggested: Private control plane + private inference nodes (2 dedicated GPU nodes for initial pilot) with autoscale to 6 on peak, KD routing to 7B fallback.
- Samir: sketch a Dedicated sizing: 2x H100-class equiv for 70B quantized baseline; A100x2 could be alternative if cost tighter. Need perf numbers from infra team for our quant kernels.

Action items (next 7 business days):
- Priya: assemble pilot SOW draft (estimate: 6w pilot, on-site net review, deliverables = perf baseline, rollout plan, KV/prompt trimming guide) — due 2025-08-20.
- Samir: perf data request to eng-serving-runtime for 7B/70B quantized p50/p95 on H100 and A100 (include streaming/kv-case) — request ticket ENG-4189.
- Clara: create onboarding checklist for customer security team (HSM flows, KMS key exchange, IP whitelisting steps) and share to Confluence.
- Customer (Derek): share sample traffic trace (1 week) and 50 example prompts + desired JSON schema.

Open questions for customer (need quick answers):
- Can they accept a small percentage (<=1%) of requests routed to hosted fallback during pilot for reliability testing, or must everything remain in-VPC?
- Exact retention policy for logs and whether redaction can be applied pre-storage (helps compliance).
- Which vector store are they planning (we recommend Milvus/Weaviate in their VPC) and approximate QPS for embedding lookups?

Rough effort / risk assessment (notes for SOW):
- Pilot build + perf validation: 4 engineers (infra + se + runtime) x 6 weeks => 12 engineer-weeks.
- Main risk drivers: HSM procurement + network config windows + tokenization consistency. If HSM delayed, we can run masked-PII proof-of-concept (no PII leaves VPC) but cannot sign artifacts.

Triage notes / quick fixes to suggest immediately:
- Client debounce: add 200ms coalescing window on mobile to aggregate small prompt bursts into one request. Low effort on client side, high win for batching efficiency.
- Server-side batching policy: enable continuous batching with max latency cap 120ms for low-latency pool; fall through to dedicated burst pool if queue grows.
- Prompt trimming rule: keep last 3 driver messages + encoded route state (hash), move older chat context into embeddings lookup, not raw prompt.

Meeting follow-ups scheduled:
- 2025-08-19 network sync with their infra (Clara + their net lead).
- 2025-08-22 kickoff SOW review (internal) with Samir + product manager.

Personal notes / scribbles (todo later):
- Run quick Jupyter test with our 4-bit kernels on sample prompts to validate latency vs memory before SOW finalization.
- Add automated prompt-size gating to Redwood SDK to emit warnings when token budgets exceed recommended thresholds.
- Build a short one-pager for Derek summarizing the tradeoffs 70B vs 7B for cost/latency with clear decision points.
